subject: Heat Transfer
summary: the fin equation, long and insulated-tip fins, corrected length, fin efficiency and effectiveness, lumped-capacitance (Biot number, time constant), Fourier number, Heisler charts and the semi-infinite solid

questions.text: The basic assumption of the lumped capacitance method of transient conduction is that
opts: the heat transfer coefficient is zero
the temperature of the body is uniform in space at every instant and changes only with time
questions.ans: (C) the temperature of the body is uniform in space at every instant and changes only with time
solution: Concept: When internal conduction resistance is negligible (Bi < 0.1), spatial temperature differences inside the body are small.
Then T = T(t) only, and an energy balance gives ρVc dT/dt = −hA<sub>s</sub>(T − T<sub>∞</sub>).
Solution: θ/θ<sub>i</sub> = exp(−t/τ) with τ = ρVc/(hA<sub>s</sub>).
Exam tip: Always check Bi = hLc/k with Lc = V/As before using the lumped formula.

questions.text: A long steel cylinder of 40 mm diameter (k = 15 W/m·K) is cooled in a fluid with h = 60 W/m²·K. The Biot number based on the lumped characteristic length (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Lumped Bi uses Lc = V/As; for a long cylinder Lc = πR²L/(2πRL) = R/2.
Bi = hLc/k = 60 × 0.01/15 = 0.04 (< 0.1, so lumped analysis is valid)
Exam tip: Heisler charts use Lc = R (not R/2) for cylinders; do not mix the two definitions.

questions.text: A copper sphere of 30 mm diameter (ρ = 8900 kg/m³, c = 385 J/kg·K, k = 400 W/m·K) at 200 °C is cooled in air at 25 °C with h = 25 W/m²·K. The time for it to reach 80 °C (in s, round off to the nearest integer) is ______
solution: Concept: Bi = h(D/6)/k = 25 × 0.005/400 = 0.0003 < 0.1, so lumped: t = τ ln(θi/θ).
Exam tip: Work with temperature excesses θ = T − T∞, never with T directly.

questions.text: To make a thermocouple respond faster to temperature changes in a gas stream, one should
opts: use a smaller bead and increase the gas velocity
use a bead material of higher density and specific heat
questions.ans: (B) use a smaller bead and increase the gas velocity
solution: Concept: Time constant τ = ρcV/(hAs) = ρcD/(6h) for a spherical bead.
A smaller D reduces τ directly; a higher gas velocity raises h and reduces τ further.
Higher ρc (option C) or lower velocity (option D) would slow the response.
Exam tip: After one τ the bead has covered 63.2 % of the step change; after 5τ, over 99 %.

questions.text: A very long brass rod of 8 mm diameter (k = 110 W/m·K) projects from a furnace wall into air with h = 15 W/m²·K, as shown. Its base is 60 °C above the air temperature. The heat lost by the rod (in W, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Infinitely long fin: Q = √(hPkAc) θb, with the temperature excess falling as θ = θbe−mx.
Exam tip: m = √(4h/(kD)) = 8.26 m⁻¹ here, so a rod longer than about 3/m ≈ 0.36 m already acts as 'infinite'.

questions.text: Fin effectiveness is defined as the ratio of
opts: heat transfer from the fin to the heat that would be transferred from the base area alone without the fin
heat transfer from the fin to the heat it would transfer if the whole fin were at base temperature
fin surface area to base area
questions.ans: (A) heat transfer from the fin to the heat that would be transferred from the base area alone without the fin
solution: Concept: Effectiveness εf = Qfin/(hAcθb), the gain over the bare base.
Option (B) is the definition of fin efficiency η<sub>f</sub>, a different quantity.
Fins are justified only when ε<sub>f</sub> is well above 1 (≥ 2 in practice).
Exam tip: For a long fin, εf = √(kP/(hAc)), so thin, closely spaced, high-k fins in gases work best.

questions.text: A straight rectangular aluminium fin (k = 200 W/m·K) is 2 mm thick and 20 mm long; h = 50 W/m²·K. Using the corrected length L<sub>c</sub> = L + t/2 with an insulated-tip formula, the fin efficiency (in %, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: For a thin rectangular fin (width ≫ t), m = √(2h/(kt)); the convecting tip is handled by extending the length by t/2.
Exam tip: For a pin fin the corrected length is L + D/4.

questions.text: In a very long fin, the temperature excess θ = T − T<sub>∞</sub> varies along the fin length x as
solution: Concept: The fin equation d²θ/dx² − m²θ = 0 has solution θ = C₁emx + C₂e−mx.
For an infinitely long fin θ → 0 as x → ∞, so C₁ = 0 and C₂ = θ<sub>b</sub>.
Hence θ = θbe−mx, an exponential decay.
Exam tip: For an insulated tip, θ/θb = cosh m(L − x)/cosh mL.

questions.text: A steel ball of 40 mm diameter (ρ = 7800 kg/m³, c = 460 J/kg·K, k = 40 W/m·K) at 420 °C is placed in air at 20 °C with h = 40 W/m²·K. The heat it loses in the first 300 s (in kJ, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Bi = h(D/6)/k = 40 × 0.00667/40 = 0.0067, so lumped. Heat lost in time t: Q = mcθi(1 − e−t/τ).
Exam tip: mcθi is the maximum heat the body can ever lose (as t → ∞).

questions.text: The one-term approximation used in the Heisler charts for transient conduction is accurate (within about 2 %) when
solution: Concept: The exact solution is an infinite series in exp(−λn²Fo); higher terms decay quickly as Fo grows.
For Fo > 0.2 only the first term matters, and the charts (θ₀/θ<sub>i</sub> versus Fo with 1/Bi as parameter) are built on it.
Bi < 0.1 is the lumped criterion, a different simplification.
Exam tip: For very short times (small Fo) treat the body as a semi-infinite solid instead.

questions.text: A large steel plate 50 mm thick (α = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ m²/s) is suddenly exposed to hot gases on both faces. The Fourier number based on the half-thickness after 10 minutes (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Fo = αt/L², with L the half-thickness for a plate heated on both sides.
Exam tip: Fo > 0.2 here, so the one-term (Heisler) solution applies.

questions.text: A thick concrete slab (α = 5 × 10⁻⁷ m²/s) is initially at 30 °C throughout. Its surface is suddenly raised to and held at 80 °C, as shown. Taking erf(0.5) = 0.5205, the temperature 60 mm below the surface after 2 hours is about
solution: Concept: Semi-infinite solid with a step change in surface temperature: (T − Ts)/(Ti − Ts) = erf[x/(2√(αt))].
Exam tip: At the surface erf(0) = 0 gives T = Ts; deep inside erf → 1 gives T = Ti.

questions.text: A tube in a heat exchanger carries water inside, while air flows over its outside. To increase the heat transfer most effectively, fins should be attached
opts: on neither side, since fins always reduce heat transfer
solution: Concept: The overall rate is limited by the larger resistance 1/(hA). Gas-side h (10–100 W/m²·K) is far lower than water-side h (thousands).
Adding area where h is low cuts the controlling resistance.
This is why car radiators and AC condensers have fins on the air side.
Exam tip: Fins pay off where hA is smallest.

questions.text: An aluminium pin fin (k = 100 W/m·K) of 4 mm diameter and 60 mm length has an insulated tip, as shown. Its base is at 100 °C and the surrounding air is at 25 °C with h = 25 W/m²·K. The tip temperature (in °C, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Insulated tip: θ(x)/θb = cosh m(L − x)/cosh mL, so at the tip θL = θb/cosh mL.
Exam tip: A tip far hotter than the air means the fin is short (mL small) and highly efficient.

questions.text: Two solid spheres of the same material, of diameters D and 2D, are cooled from the same initial temperature in the same fluid (lumped behaviour). The time taken by the larger sphere to reach a given temperature is
opts: the same as for the smaller sphere
twice that of the smaller sphere
four times that of the smaller sphere
half that of the smaller sphere
questions.ans: (B) twice that of the smaller sphere
solution: Concept: For the same θ/θi, t ∝ τ = ρcLc/h with Lc = D/6.
Doubling D doubles L<sub>c</sub> and hence τ.
So the larger sphere takes twice as long.
Exam tip: In the non-lumped (Heisler) regime, time at equal Fo scales with D² instead.
